desc.overview: How the platform is laid out and how to reach each part.

overview.step1: Sign in with your email and password; the home page IS the AI assistant.
overview.step2: Open “Echo” from the side rail to record calls and read transcripts.
overview.step3: “Management” holds members, models and skills; “Settings” holds the organization.
overview.step4: The avatar menu (top of the page) carries theme, calendar and sign-out.

assistant.step1: Type your question in the center box and press Enter.
assistant.step2: Pick the model and the skill from the two lists beside the box.
assistant.step3: Attach up to three text files with “Add file”.
assistant.step4: The microphone button turns your speech into text.
assistant.step5: “History” brings back previous conversations; answers can be rated or regenerated.

echo.step1: In “Record in browser”, pick your microphone and speaker and start recording.
echo.step2: The level bar should move as you speak; if it stays flat, check the microphone.
echo.step3: Long sessions split automatically into 30-minute parts, uploaded as you go.
echo.step4: “Pause” holds the recording; “Finish & process” hands the call to transcription.
echo.step5: Send already-recorded files from “Upload a file”; results appear under “Calls”.

management.step1: In “Users”, add a member with an invitation — the link is shown exactly once.
management.step2: Accept or reject pending requests; change each member's role right there.
management.step3: Select several rows to enable or disable members in one action.
management.step4: “Models” manages the organization's allowed model list.
management.step5: “Skills” creates and edits the assistant's ready-made instructions.

settings.step1: Theme (dark/light), language and calendar change from the avatar menu or “Settings”.
settings.step2: In “Profile”, edit your display name, Latin-script name and username — names are never translated.
settings.step3: Set your profile photo with the camera button on the circle and accept the crop.
settings.step4: “Audit logs” in Settings shows the organization's administrative actions.

desc.record: Record a session with your device microphone — 30-minute parts, uploaded as you go.
desc.upload: Upload a recorded audio file — transcription starts once it lands.
desc.archive: Archived calls — same details and actions; unarchive moves one back to Calls.
desc.speakers: People and their titles — every call page picks speakers from this list.
desc.summaries: Each recording's summary, gathered for reading.
desc.new-meeting: Record in your browser — the transcript, your notes and the action items all land on this page. To add a file you already have, use the upload icon on this menu row.

audit.codesOnly: This page says what happened, not what was said. Question text, transcripts and conversation content never enter the audit trail.

audit.failed: The audit record could not be read.
audit.unknownSourceNote: This entry is of a type this version of the interface doesn't know. We don't drop it — it is shown exactly as it arrived.
audit.adminOnlyNote: Audit records are visible to organization admins only. This does not mean there are no events — events are recorded; reading them is an admin's to do.
audit.actorRemovedNote: This person was removed from the organization and their name was erased, but what they did stays in the record — the record outlives people.

drains.intro: A drain is a signed webhook: every event carries identifiers and status only, is HMAC-signed with your secret, retried on failure, and logged below.
drains.loadFailed: Could not load the drains. Refresh to retry.
drains.saveFailed: Could not save. Please try again.
drains.adminOnly: Drains are managed by organization admins.
drains.urlHint: HTTPS endpoint that receives the events. Private and loopback addresses are refused at delivery time.
drains.secretNote: Store it now. It signs every delivery (v1 scheme, 5-minute replay tolerance) and cannot be shown again.

gateway.title: API gateway
gateway.intro: Any system can push audio in and pull transcripts, summaries and answers out — under the same permission wall you are under. The named connectors further down this page get built on this gateway later.
gateway.adminOnly: This section belongs to organization admins
gateway.adminOnlyNote: Only an admin can create and revoke keys and webhooks. If you need an integration, ask your organization's admin to create a key in your name; that key can do what you can do.
gateway.keysNote: Every key is created in one member's name and can do exactly what that member can do — no more. If that member is disabled, the key stops working the same moment, with no rotation needed.
gateway.actorNotListed: This id is not in the member list:
gateway.actorInactive: This member is disabled; the key does not work.
gateway.revokeBody: Any system using this key is refused from this moment on. The key is not deleted; its record stays with a revocation date, so what existed and when it was withdrawn remains readable. A revoked key never comes back — carrying on means minting a new one.
gateway.nameHint: So you can tell later which system uses it.
gateway.actsAsNote: This key can do exactly what you can do — no more.
gateway.actsAsLabel: Whose name is this key in?
gateway.actsAsSelectHint: The key gets exactly the access this member has. This choice cannot be changed later.
gateway.actsAsPersonNote: This key can do exactly what {name} can do — no more. If {name} is disabled, this key stops working the same moment.
gateway.actsAsSelfNote: This key can do exactly what you can do — no more. If your account is disabled, this key stops working the same moment.
gateway.allowAssistantHint: The assistant spends model tokens, and that costs money. Closed by default: a leaked or runaway key can read transcripts, but it cannot drain a model budget.
gateway.capabilitiesImmutable: A key's capabilities are decided when it is created and never change afterwards. To change them, revoke the key and mint a new one — so the record reads “one credential ended, a different one began”, rather than leaving a key whose meaning depends on when you looked.
gateway.keyOnceBody: The NeurAI platform keeps only a cryptographic fingerprint of the key, so there is no way to show it again. If you close this without saving it somewhere, the only way forward is to revoke it and create a new one.
gateway.keySaved: I have saved the key somewhere safe
gateway.webhooksNote: A webhook is a doorbell, not a delivery: it only tells you which event happened to which call. Transcript and summary text is never sent — to read content, come back through this gateway, under the same permission wall and the same audit trail.
gateway.pauseNote: Pausing keeps the webhook and its delivery history; nothing is deleted.
gateway.urlHint: https only. Private-network and loopback addresses are refused.
gateway.urlInvalid: The URL must start with https://.
gateway.eventsHint: Pick at least one event. The list is closed — you cannot type a new one, because subscribing to a typo means nothing ever arrives and nobody can tell why.
gateway.eventsRequired: At least one event is required.
gateway.secretOnceBody: You use this secret to verify the signature on each delivery, so you can be sure it came from NeurAI. NeurAI does not show it again.
gateway.secretSaved: I have saved the secret somewhere safe
gateway.deliveriesNote: Only identifiers and status are recorded here; there is no content involved.
gateway.copyFailed: Copy failed — select the text and copy it by hand.

legal.ownershipBody: Audio you record or upload, its transcripts, and everything derived from them belong to your organization. The transcript is the source of truth; derived artifacts are rebuildable and carry their provenance.
legal.accessBody: Every read and write - including every action of the AI assistant - runs under the requesting member’s own permissions, enforced at the database layer. Nobody, including the assistant, can reach content its caller could not.
legal.processingBody: Speech is transcribed and summarized using the model providers your organization’s admin allows. Model providers receive the content needed to perform the requested task and nothing else.
legal.retentionBody: Deleting a call hides it immediately and permanently purges its audio, transcript and derivatives after the retention window. Conversations with the assistant are archived, never silently deleted.
legal.securityBody: Sessions are httpOnly cookies; tokens never transit the browser. Content never appears in logs. Outbound webhooks carry identifiers and status only, signed with your secret.
legal.changesBody: A revision of these terms changes the version date above. The text never changes silently.

tour.label: Guided walkthrough
tour.lessonRecord: How do I record a meeting?
tour.lessonUpload: How do I add an existing file?
tour.lessonAsk: How do I find and ask?
tour.rec1: Everything starts here — New meeting is where a recording begins. Press it.
tour.rec2: Pick your microphone and test it with the meter, so the meeting is never silent by surprise.
tour.rec3: Choose the meeting's language, a summary template, and — if you want — the model that will write the summary.
tour.rec4: Press Start recording. You can leave this page: the recording follows you in the top bar.
tour.up1: Already have a recording? This icon uploads a file straight into the pipeline — no form in between.
tour.up2: It lands in Records with everything else, transcribed and summarised the same way.
tour.ask1: Records is where every meeting lives — open any row to read its summary and transcript.
tour.ask2: Search looks across every transcript you are allowed to see, and shows the exact sentence.
tour.ask3: And this is the assistant — ask it anything about your meetings, in your own words.
